body:
Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. ((NCDL)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending delivered a broadly constructive quarter, with distribution coverage, stronger originations, growing platform activity and solid credit metrics standing out. Those positives outweighed lower net investment income, realized losses, a modest NAV decline, a larger watch list and continued pressure from selective deal markets and broader economic risks.

Distribution Remained Fully Covered

Third-quarter net investment income was $0.38 per share, while adjusted net investment income was $0.39 per share. Both measures covered the regular quarterly distribution of $0.36 per share, supporting the company’s income-focused appeal.

Supplemental Payment Lifted Fourth-Quarter Distribution

The board declared a total fourth-quarter distribution of $0.38 per share. It includes the regular $0.36 payment and a $0.02 supplemental distribution, providing an additional benefit to shareholders.

Originations Rebounded Sharply

Gross originations rose to approximately $213 million in the third quarter from just $12 million in the second quarter. The increase included $93 million of Joint Venture commitments and $120 million committed to new transactions.

Joint Venture Expanded Deployment Capacity

NCDL completed a Joint Venture with an institutional partner and sold about $150 million of first lien loans into it. At September 30, the venture held $147.5 million of investments, carried a 9.2% weighted average yield and generated a 13.6% annualized return on NCDL’s investment during the quarter.

Churchill Platform Activity Stayed Strong

The Churchill platform closed or committed to more than 90 transactions totaling roughly $5 billion during the quarter. Over 80% of deployment went to senior direct lending, even as private equity mergers and acquisitions remained relatively slow.

Credit Metrics Remained Healthy

Traditional middle-market first lien borrowers reported total net leverage of 5.2 times and interest coverage of 2.3 times. Management attributed those figures to conservative loan structures and relatively low attachment points.

Nonaccruals Were Broadly Stable

One portfolio company entered nonaccrual status during the quarter. The investment had a cost basis of $3.9 million and a fair value of $3.1 million, underscoring the need to monitor weaker credits despite stable overall nonaccrual levels.

Portfolio Diversification Improved

The portfolio grew to 258 companies from 244 at the end of the second quarter. The 10 largest holdings accounted for 12.4% of fair value, the largest exposure was 1.6% and the average position was only 0.4%.

Balance-Sheet Leverage Declined

Gross debt-to-equity fell to 1.23 times from 1.29 times, while net debt-to-equity dropped to 1.17 times from 1.23 times. The primary driver was the sale of assets into the Joint Venture, which reduced leverage on NCDL’s balance sheet.

Weighted Average Yield Increased

The weighted average yield on debt and income-producing investments at cost rose to 9.7% from 9.3%. Higher base rates at quarter-end and the accretive benefits of the Joint Venture investment supported the improvement.

Senior Loans Remained the Core Allocation

First lien loans represented 87.1% of the total portfolio at September 30. Junior debt accounted for 7.6%, equity for 3.1% and the Joint Venture for 2.2%, with the venture primarily focused on first lien loans.

Equity Realization Generated a Gain

A $2 million realized gain from an equity investment partly offset the quarter’s realized losses. Management said the investment was held for three to four years, generated more than twice invested capital and produced an internal rate of return of about 20%.

Management Emphasized Equity Co-Investments

NCDL is directing more capital toward equity co-investments rather than junior debt. The strategy is intended to modestly increase portfolio equity and support capital appreciation while preserving the share of senior loan investments.

Unsecured Notes Tap Added Capital

NCDL completed a $100 million tap of its existing 2030 unsecured notes, bringing total unsecured notes issued to $400 million. TIAA purchased all of the new notes, which management described as evidence of continued parent-company support.

After quarter-end through October 30, the company bought approximately 278,000 shares at an average price of about $10.76. The purchases totaled roughly $3 million, leaving $47 million available under the $50 million repurchase authorization.

Management Saw Attractive Financing Opportunities

Management said NCDL continues to find attractive financing opportunities in the middle market. It highlighted proprietary sourcing, an experienced team, strong relationships, scale and more than two decades of Churchill experience as competitive advantages.

Net Investment Income Fell Sequentially

Third-quarter net investment income declined to $0.38 per share from $0.41 per share in the prior quarter. The change was primarily linked to a higher incentive fee, while adjusted results also included a one-time expense of about $0.01 per share tied to accelerated deferred financing costs.

Total Investment Income Edged Lower

Total investment income decreased modestly to $43.7 million from $44.3 million in the second quarter. Management attributed the decline mainly to a small reduction in the size of the investment portfolio.

Realized Losses Reduced Quarterly Net Income

GAAP net income was $0.32 per share, including $0.06 per share of net realized and unrealized losses. Net realized losses totaled $0.08 per share and mainly reflected amendments and restructurings involving two underperforming debt positions.

Net asset value fell to $17.13 per share from $17.19 per share, a 0.3% quarter-over-quarter decline. The change largely reflected the effect of net realized and unrealized losses during the period.

The internal watch list rose to 11.6% of fair value from 10.8% at the end of the second quarter. Two new additions drove the increase, while the weighted average internal risk rating remained unchanged at 4.4.

One New Nonaccrual Was Added

Private Equity Deal Activity Stayed Selective

U.S. private equity deal count and value increased from the second quarter, but leveraged buyout activity remained light compared with more normal periods. Management cited market volatility, high borrowing costs, geopolitical uncertainty and disruption from artificial intelligence.

Macroeconomic Risks Remained Elevated

Management pointed to inflationary pressure linked to geopolitical tensions, artificial intelligence disruption and exposure to software companies. It also cited elevated redemption activity in private business development companies and inflation remaining above the central bank’s 2% target.

Direct Lending Spreads Stabilized

Spreads for traditional first lien loans settled into a range of 475 to 500 basis points over the relevant reference rate after modest widening earlier in the year. The average spread on new first lien loans was approximately 480 basis points.

Repurchases Will Depend on the Share Price

Management said the repurchase program became active as NCDL’s share price declined. Future purchases are expected to depend on market trading, with activity designed to increase when the discount to NAV becomes wider.

Guidance Points to Joint Venture Growth

Management expects the Joint Venture to build toward a portfolio of approximately $300 million over the coming quarters and believes full deployment within 12 months is achievable. NCDL expects BDC leverage near the upper end of its 1.0-to-1.25-times target range, Joint Venture leverage of about 2.25 times and a portfolio with roughly 90% or more in senior loans.

Overall, NCDL’s call showed a company balancing reliable shareholder income and improving deployment with moderate credit pressure and uncertain markets. The Joint Venture, diversified portfolio, lower leverage and strong senior-lending focus were key positives, while weaker income, realized losses and a larger watch list remain important risks for investors.
